1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.

2. The application stands disposed of.
W.P.(CRL) 2687/2023 3.

The present petition has been filed seeking quashing of FIR No.381/2020 under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) registered at Police Station Malviya Nagar on the ground of settlement.
4. The petitioner no.1 is the husband of the respondent no.2 and the petitioners no. 2 to 5 are family members of the petitioner no.1.

sentences.text: Dispute arose between the petitioners and the respondent no.2, which resulted in filing of the present FIR by the respondent no.2 against the petitioners.

6. Now the parties have settled all their disputes before the Counselling Cell, Family Courts, Saket (South), Delhi in terms of Settlement Deed dated 7th August, 2023 which has been filed as Annexure 2 to the petition.

entities.text: Counselling Cell, Family Courts, Saket (South), Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Subsequently, parties have obtained divorce by mutual consent.
7. Issue notice.
8. Notice is accepted by the learned Standing Counsel appearing on behalf of the State and the counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent no.2.
9. The respondent no.2 is present in Court and has been identified by her counsel as well as by the Investigating Officer (IO).
She informs the Court that she has settled the matter of her own free will and without any coercion.
She further states that she has no objection to quashing of the FIR.
10. The petitioners are also present in Court and have been identified by their counsel.
They affirm the statement of the respondent no. 2 and undertake to abide by the terms of settlement arrived at between the parties.
11. As per the settlement, a sum of Rs.3,50,000/- was payable to the respondent no.2.
Out of the aforesaid amount, a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- has already been paid.
The petitioners have brought a demand draft of Rs.2,00,000/- in Court today and the same has been handed over to the respondent no.2.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 20/09/2023 at 23:13:29 12.

Considering the above settlement between the parties and the chances of conviction of the petitioner being remote and bleak, there is no use continuing with proceedings of the present FIR as it would be a misuse of the process of the Court and an unnecessary burden on the State exchequer.
Hence, it would be in the interest of justice to quash the aforementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
13. Consequently, the FIR No. 381/2020 registered at Police Station Malviya Nagar and the proceedings pursuant thereto are quashed.
14. The petition stands disposed of.
AMIT BANSAL, J SEPTEMBER 19, 2023 sr
